purpose: Research evidence and contextual semantics, not a simulation ontology

claims.Claim: Measured é properties are not descriptions of complete residential groups.
claims.Nippur context: TA 184; X 1 / XA 1 retained as catalogued
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Contextual reading of measured plots and fixtures.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Some other uses of é can be broader; no exclusive dictionary definition is proposed.
claims.Generalization limit: These sale/exchange objects only.
claims.Project relevance: Separates premises from people.

claims.Claim: Residence can be stated explicitly rather than inferred from an é–person association.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Relative clause ša ina é ... wašbu supports a residence assertion.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: The preceding a-si-rum may be a name; its status interpretation is unresolved.
claims.Generalization limit: Named relation in this account, not a census.
claims.Project relevance: Distinguishes occupancy from property relations.

claims.Claim: ḫa-la labels allocations of different kinds, including temporal temple-associated shares.
claims.Period/date: Old Babylonian; Rim-Sin 54 for office division
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Compare objects before selecting “share” or “inheritance portion.”
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Undated/damaged plot division does not establish its occasion.
claims.Generalization limit: Not every possible sense of ḫa-la.
claims.Project relevance: Avoids deriving a transaction type from one noun.

claims.Claim: A living father’s division can be combined with conditional heirship and annual support.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: The propositions coexist in the same document.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Damaged obv. 9; actual delivery and broader motives unproved.
claims.Generalization limit: One instrument; not a universal succession regime.
claims.Project relevance: Separates allocation, affiliation, obligation and performance.

claims.Claim: Kinship expressions in affiliation instruments cannot by themselves establish biological relationships.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Relationships can be constituted or restated within the instrument.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: This does not make every patronymic adoptive or fictitious.
claims.Generalization limit: Relation-specific conclusion; not a reconstructed genealogy.
claims.Project relevance: Prevents equating expressed affiliation with biological descent.

claims.Claim: Conditional repudiation clauses are provisions, not evidence that repudiation or its penalty occurred.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Distinguish condition, sanction and reported event.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Fragmentary texts cannot supply missing outcomes.
claims.Generalization limit: Documentary statement level.
claims.Project relevance: Avoids converting legal scenarios into personal biographies.

claims.Claim: A woman’s kinship and deity-linked title can be stated together with a maintenance entitlement.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: nin₉ and LUKUR Ninurta are simultaneous descriptions.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Not all similarly named women are this person.
claims.Generalization limit: One agreement; no citywide rule for titled women.
claims.Project relevance: Shows why kinship, title and entitlement should not be synonyms.

claims.Claim: The maintenance agreement’s alienation restriction does not yield an uncontested modern usufruct category.
claims.Secondary interpretation: Van Wyk 2014 discusses competing readings of whose field is restricted.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Field possessive and legal reconstruction remain disputed.
claims.Generalization limit: Competing interpretations, not an adjudication.
claims.Project relevance: Preserves uncertainty about the rights involved.

claims.Claim: Annual payment terminology is not confined to remuneration for labor.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: a₂ with annual wording occurs in distinct obligation contexts.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Neither occurrence establishes an employer–employee relation.
claims.Generalization limit: These clauses; no full lexical history of a₂.
claims.Project relevance: Prevents translating all support or rent as wages.

claims.Claim: Receipt language and explicit interest exclusions identify obligations, not a permanent social class.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: šu-ti and máš₂ nu-ub-tuku specify receipt and exclusion of interest.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Catalogue commodity discrepancy in no. 65; no inference of charitable motive.
claims.Generalization limit: The written loans only.
claims.Project relevance: Separates debtor role, financial terms and personal status.

claims.Claim: A manumission-related instrument distinguishes lifetime service from heirs’ later slave-status claims.
claims.Secondary interpretation: Stone 1987 indexes a freeing; surviving nam-geme₂ and temporal clauses support the distinction.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Release expression restored and queried; marriage/document clause damaged.
claims.Generalization limit: One damaged act; not unrestricted freedom or a general law.
claims.Project relevance: Separates juridical status, duties and time.

claims.Claim: ARAD in a divine seal formula or personal name is insufficient evidence of a person’s slave status.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Personal-name and devotional uses differ from an explicit status predication.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: ARAD can denote human slavery in other contexts; the caution does not erase it.
claims.Generalization limit: These onomastic/formulaic occurrences.
claims.Project relevance: Prevents false status assignments.

claims.Claim: Temple-linked rights could be described in temporal portions and transferred.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Four-month allocations and sales of day-defined entitlements differ from wages.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: No proof of actual personal performance or net income.
claims.Generalization limit: These transactions; not every temple office.
claims.Project relevance: Distinguishes rights, rotation, price and work.

claims.Claim: A Nuska-temple office sale combines annual days and an associated field.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: The bundle includes nam-gudu₄ / nam-lunga, a five-day annual turn and land.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Some titles/field wording damaged; exact tenure and duties unresolved.
claims.Generalization limit: One bundle, not a standard prebend definition.
claims.Project relevance: Avoids reducing institutional rights to a job title or cash salary.

claims.Claim: An office title attached to a participant does not itself identify an institution as the contracting party.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: The named buyer/borrower bears nu-eš₃ or agrig.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Institutional capacity could require other evidence; its absence is not disproved here.
claims.Generalization limit: Capacity remains unestablished, not necessarily private.
claims.Project relevance: Avoids automatic temple ownership of title-holders’ assets.

claims.Claim: A single instrument can combine Akkadian syntax/verbs with Sumerian-written legal expressions.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: ana, kīma, ilqêma/inaddin coexist with logograms/formulae.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Spoken language and scribal bilingual competence are not recoverable from this alone.
claims.Generalization limit: Written linguistic behavior in this document.
claims.Project relevance: Separates script, clause language and vernacular inference.

claims.Claim: A Nippur school witness can attest legal vocabulary without certifying a contemporary legal event.
claims.Secondary interpretation: Spada 2014 lists the witness among Nippur school legal texts.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Didactic transmission need not imply entirely invented historical content.
claims.Generalization limit: Vocabulary and textual transmission; no event count.
claims.Project relevance: Keeps model cases distinct from functional records.

claims.Claim: Findspot proximity does not securely identify all parties to a text as occupants of the excavated house.
claims.Period/date: OB tablets of different regnal dates
claims.Secondary interpretation: Stone questions links where rental parties lack patronymics and the property is nonspecific.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Some archive/house links may be strong; this is not blanket rejection of contextual archaeology.
claims.Generalization limit: Specific association problem, not all Nippur finds.
claims.Project relevance: Controls household reconstruction from text location.

claims.Claim: Seller-and-heir non-claim clauses express protection against claims, not an enumeration of current children.
claims.Primary evidence: [SAOC 44, 17, rev. closure](https://cdli.earth/P283587); [SAOC 44, 43, rev. closure](https://cdli.earth/P283584); [SAOC 44, 46, rev. closure](https://cdli.earth/P283588)
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: ibila can appear prospectively in a conveyance formula.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Its interpretation is not identical to named heirs in a division.
claims.Generalization limit: These legal clauses.
claims.Project relevance: Prevents deriving a household census from legal closure.

claims.Claim: An elder-brother designation can accompany a special allocation without proving universal primogeniture.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: nam-šeš-gal-la and šeš-gal qualify the allocation.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Quantification and genealogical reconstructions need additional checking.
claims.Generalization limit: This distinction in this instrument only.
claims.Project relevance: Separates local allocation from a citywide succession rule.

claims.Claim: The surviving multi-year field arrangement is insufficient to classify a permanent labor status.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: Three-year and fourth-year clauses are legible but obligations damaged.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: A fuller collation may recover performance terms.
claims.Generalization limit: Negative evidentiary conclusion about this damaged record.
claims.Project relevance: Keeps land use, contractual tasks and personal status distinct.

claims.Claim: Transaction clauses can identify an exchange more precisely than a generic catalogue “sale” label.
claims.Secondary interpretation: This return’s reading: ki ba-gar-ra and balancing payment identify the transaction’s structure.
claims.Counterevidence/disagreement: Associated persons and date do not make adjacent editions duplicates.
claims.Generalization limit: This catalogue/text comparison.
claims.Project relevance: Prevents classification from metadata alone.

semantic_cautions.Language: Sumerian; É also a logogram in Akkadian contexts
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Measured real estate, with fixtures specified separately.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Extent of the transferred built unit is document-specific.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: One word does not identify a nuclear family or all occupants.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Property identification or reference point.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Ownership, use and residence require clause-level evidence.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Every named house is not a residence of its named associate.

semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: Who resides in the house of ...
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Express residence statement.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: a-si-rum before the clause is unresolved as name/status.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Residence alone still does not prove kinship or permanent membership.

semantic_cautions.Term/form: níĝ gu₂-na é gál-la / comparable contents formulae
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Moveable contents distinguished from measured real estate.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Readings and scope of contents differ between editions/texts.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: “Estate” should not silently include every asset, person and debt.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Distinct land descriptions in particular instruments.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Physical condition and title cannot be inferred from a bare gloss.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: A single modern “landholding” label can conceal different objects.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Affiliation and descent designation.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Biology and age are not established by the noun alone.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: “Child” does not necessarily mean minor; patronymic is not a full family tree.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Relations expressed within allocation/support arrangements.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Legal affiliation may matter alongside descent.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: No automatic biological siblinghood or co-residence.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Seniority designation connected to an allocation.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Not a fully established universal rule of precedence.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: “Primogeniture” adds more than the phrase demonstrates.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Parental relations recognized or conditionally repudiated.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Fragmentary relationships need reconstruction.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not force every occurrence into biological parentage.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Relational spouse term; referent determines husband/wife translation.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: School and functional uses remain separate.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not invariably translate DAM as “wife.”

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Marriage provision in a combined affiliation instrument.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Ceremony, residence and household authority are not detailed.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Marriage wording is not a complete account of marriage practice.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Constitutive affiliation and succession wording.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Local damaged forms must not be replaced by an ideal template.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Adoption does not automatically mean either infant rescue or merely a commercial fiction.

semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: You are not my child / mother
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Conditional repudiation language.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Accompanying penalties and parties are partly broken.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not evidence that the declaration was actually made.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Named entitlement or future successor in a clause.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Scope differs between support and sale texts.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not always eldest biological son or an already inherited estate.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Status that heirs are barred from claiming under stated temporal conditions.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Surrounding clauses damaged.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Generic “dependent” would erase explicit slave-status wording; “free of all duties” would also overstate.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Editor’s restoration in a freeing-related act.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Bracketed and queried, not fully preserved.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not quote it as a securely visible local technical term.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Continuing attendance/service provision.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Extent and coerciveness of performance unspecified.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Service, slavery and perpetual household membership are not identical propositions.

semantic_cautions.Term/form: ARAD₂ + deity; ARAD₂ in personal name
semantic_cautions.Language: Sumerian writing / name or seal formula
semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: Servant of deity; theophoric name element
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Devotional and onomastic use.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Must distinguish full names from independent predicates.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not independent evidence of an enslaved seal owner or scribe.

semantic_cautions.Language: Sumerian writing in a didactic text
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Explicit human relation within a narrated case.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Does not independently prove the historical person’s status at the copy date.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not erase slavery, but do not count a school narrative as a status census.

semantic_cautions.Language: Sumerian title spelling; often rendered nadītu in scholarship
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Title coexisting with kinship and property-related participation.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Akkadian conventional rendering is not a phonetic spelling in these clauses.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not automatically “nun,” “prostitute,” slave, or the Sippar institution.
semantic_cautions.Confidence: HIGH for title; MODERATE for institutional reconstruction

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Recurrent support entitlement.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: “Rations” can sound administrative even in a family agreement.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: An allocation does not itself identify an employee.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Rental consideration or parental support in the cited contexts.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Spellings/reading conventions differ.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not translate automatically as salary or wage.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Allocation noun with more than one type of object.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Occasion may be uncertain in a damaged division.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not an automatic marker of post-mortem inheritance.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Receipt in loans; legal effect follows object and construction.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Other constructions can concern adoption; not one invariant legal operation.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Receipt, adoption and ownership are not interchangeable.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Express interest exclusion.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Reason for exclusion unstated.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not infer charity, kinship, or a universal zero-interest rule.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Sale and consideration, including an office entitlement.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Price differs from revenue or wage.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: “Bought” alone does not define a modern unrestricted ownership doctrine.

semantic_cautions.Term/form: ki ba-gar-ra; é é-e gin₇ / é ki-ma é
semantic_cautions.Language: Sumerian / Akkadian kīma in mixed wording
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Exchange with or without a balancing silver payment.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Catalogue “sale” can be too broad.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Silver consideration does not make every conveyance a simple sale.

semantic_cautions.Term/form: inim nu-...-gá-gá; seller and ibila closure
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Exclusion of later assertions by stated parties/successors.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Range of possible third-party claims needs other clauses.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not a register of current children; not proof that all conceivable rights are extinguished.

semantic_cautions.Term/form: gín with é area / gín kù-babbar
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Homographic unit language distinguished by object/system.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Conversion not attempted in this report.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Never compare land-area and silver-weight numerals as one quantity.

semantic_cautions.Term/form: mu 3-kam; mu 4-kam in a field arrangement
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Temporal differentiation of land-use terms.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Damaged obligation clauses.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not reconstruct a complete labor contract from its duration alone.

semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: Dais/platform and seat designations associated with deities
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Temple-associated rights divided into four-month shares.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Precise duty and institutional meaning not independently resolved.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not necessarily sale of furniture or a complete job description.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Sale object quantified in days.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Initial nam restored; garza₂ requires contextual interpretation.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: An acquired entitlement is not proof its owner personally worked every turn.
semantic_cautions.Confidence: HIGH for sale; MODERATE for full semantics

semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: House-supervision, gatekeeping and another technical office
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Several office designations bundled in one transfer.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Opening/institutional names damaged; bur-šu-ma not resolved.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Do not invent a modern hierarchy or function for an uncertain title.

semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: Cult office; brewing-related office; Nuska temple
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Office rights, annual days and field in one instrument.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Full duty set and associated field expression uncertain.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not simply a priest’s or brewer’s modern employment contract.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Temporal entitlement/rotation language.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Actual performance and income not documented by the formula.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: A time-share of rights is not a headcount or wage rate.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Appositions identifying parties.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Precise capacity in the transaction is unstated.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Title-holder is not automatically an institutional agent.

semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: Local official; herald; administrator; military title
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Titles attached to named participants/witnesses.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Authority, jurisdiction and delegated capacity are not specified.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: “Mayor,” “manager,” or “police” can import modern powers.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Different professional/service descriptions.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: A witness list is not an organizational chart.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Occupation does not exhaust status, kinship or household relations.

semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Collective judicial authority in a school narrative.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: No independently established proceedings/date in this witness.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Not a modern jury or parliament; not an observed court roster.

semantic_cautions.Group: F. Written language and legal expression
semantic_cautions.Literal/common gloss: To/for; like/in exchange; took-and; gives/will give
semantic_cautions.Semantic range: Akkadian syntax and finite verbs alongside logograms.
semantic_cautions.Disputed points: Different surfaces must be compared rather than homogenized.
semantic_cautions.Misleading English assumptions to avoid: Sumerian signs do not by themselves make every clause Sumerian.
